failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Stats, inventory, tools, class abilities, and combat are all cosmetic. Skill checks are decorative (d20 rolls don't meaningfully gate anything). SP/stamina is never spent. Leveling has no effect beyond HP/SP restore. The RPG layer is pure decoration.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Make RPG mechanics functional: (1) Skill checks must gate encounter paths — high Circuit Analysis lets you skip calculation steps, high Intuition gives clues. (2) Tools must be mechanically required — Multimeter to read voltages, Oscilloscope to see waveforms, Logic Analyzer to decode protocols. Without the right tool, certain encounters are harder or locked. (3) Inventory must be consumable — player selects components FROM inventory to solve puzzles, and wrong selection wastes the component. (4) SP must be spendable — spend SP to get hints, retry failed checks, or use class abilities. (5) Implement at least one class ability per specialization.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Zone 1 has 4 good encounters but Zones 2-5 are skeletal (1-2 encounters each). Only 1 quiz question imported from 184 documents — the regex doesn't match actual note formats. Scaffolding doesn't fade across zones. No adaptive difficulty.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Fix the quiz question extraction regex to capture the actual 'Test Your Understanding' format in the notes (look for Q&A under <details> tags and **bold** question patterns). Each zone needs 3-4 full encounters matching the design spec depth — Zone 2 should have pull-ups, address conflict, bus capacitance, and level shifting. Zone 3: termination, protocol selection, transceiver failure, priority inversion. Zone 4: clock modes, chip select, speed tradeoffs, protocol comparison. Zone 5: decoupling, ground loops, full diagnosis chain. Scaffolding should fade: Zone 1 shows formulas, Zone 2 shows partial hints, Zone 3+ gives only symptoms.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: Engagement drops sharply after Zone 1. Encounters become formulaic: see problem → click answer → gain XP. Inventory is non-functional. Tools don't matter. No exploration. Skill checks are decorative.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Tie motivation to intrinsic game mechanics: (1) Make encounters feel different — some require using tools (oscilloscope shows waveform you must interpret), some require inventory selection, some require skill checks that actually matter. (2) Add a 'supply closet' where players can browse/buy components with gold. (3) Let players choose encounter order within a zone. (4) Add side encounters that use spaced repetition from the DB (NPC asks about a fading mastery topic). (5) Make Doc respond to the player's specific specialization differently.

failing_dimensions.evaluator_finding: No ARIA landmark roles on game regions, no aria-live for state changes, color-only message differentiation, no alt text for ASCII diagrams, help button too small.
failing_dimensions.action_required: Add: (1) role='main' on narrative, role='complementary' on HUD, role='navigation' on actions. (2) aria-live='polite' on the narrative area so screen readers announce new messages. (3) Add text prefixes to messages (e.g., 'SUCCESS: ...' or 'WARNING: ...') alongside color. (4) Add aria-label descriptions to ASCII circuit diagrams. (5) Make help button at least 44px. (6) Add a persistent text-size control (+/- buttons).

passing_dimensions.preserve: Circuit diagnosis IS the gameplay. Calculating R6, selecting capacitor ratings, understanding inductor saturation — all intrinsically integrated. Do NOT add quiz gates or separate the learning from the gameplay.
Pupper repair framing works. Zone progression through subsystems is natural. Doc as mentor is good. Keep the zone structure and narrative voice.
LLM evaluation via /api/evaluate-llm is excellent. Freeform text input + suggested buttons. Misconception detection. Keep this hybrid approach.
Clean free/premium boundary. No friction, no gates, no ads. Premium zones are clearly optional. Keep this approach.

biggest_risk: RPG mechanics are purely cosmetic — stats, inventory, tools, and class abilities have no mechanical effect, making the game feel like a linear quiz with RPG decorations
